record.paper_title: Problèmes ouverts en théorie des intersections
record.context_brief: integral comparison of Chow and K-theory gradeds
record.original_question: For a smooth quasi-projective scheme X over a field, let A(X) be the Chow ring, let Gr'_top(X) be the graded ring associated with the topological filtration by codimension of supports on K'(X), and let Gr'(X) be the graded ring associated with the λ-filtration. Are the comparison formulas between A(X), Gr'_top(X), and Gr'(X) true integrally, not merely modulo torsion? Equivalently, are the formulas labeled (4.4) and (4.5), relating the maps φ:A(X)→Gr'_top(X) and ψ:Gr'_top(X)→A(X), valid exactly rather than only modulo torsion, so that in particular φ^2:A^2(X)→Gr'_top^2(X) is an isomorphism? Later notes in the source report that the relevant formulas were established without neglecting torsion by Mumford and Jouanolou.

evidence.quote: Il semble assez plausible que les formules (4.4) soient vraies telles quelles et non seulement modulo torsion, ou ce qui revient au même, que la formule 4.5. soit vraie non seulement modulo torsion.
Sauf erreur, le fait que φ^2 soit un isomorphisme n'est pas prouvé à l'heure actuelle, même dans le cas particulier où dim X = 3.
J.P. JOUANOLOU vient de prouver ces formules pour tout y sans négliger la torsion.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a smooth quasi-projective scheme over a field. Denote by $A(X) =  igoplus_p A^p(X)$ the Chow ring of cycles modulo rational equivalence, graded by codimension. Let $K'(X) = K_0'(X)$ be the Grothendieck group of coherent sheaves on $X$ (which, by smoothness, coincides with $K_0(X)$ and is a ring). Equip $K'(X)$ with two decreasing filtrations:

(i) the topological filtration by codimension of supports, $F^p_{\mathrm{top}} K'(X)$, generated by classes of coherent sheaves whose support has codimension $\geq p$, with associated graded ring $\mathrm{Gr}'_{\mathrm{top}}(X)$;

(ii) the $\lambda$-filtration (Grothendieck's $\gamma$-filtration) $F^p_\gamma K'(X)$, with associated graded ring $\mathrm{Gr}'(X)$.

There are natural ring homomorphisms
$$\varphi : A(X) \longrightarrow \mathrm{Gr}'_{\mathrm{top}}(X), \qquad \psi : \mathrm{Gr}'_{\mathrm{top}}(X) \longrightarrow A(X),$$
whose compositions in either order equal multiplication by an integer factor (built from $(p-1)!$ in codimension $p$) modulo torsion, in the standard comparison formulas linking $A(X)$, $\mathrm{Gr}'_{\mathrm{top}}(X)$, and $\mathrm{Gr}'(X)$.

Question: Do these comparison formulas relating $\varphi$ and $\psi$ hold exactly (integrally), and not merely modulo torsion? In particular, is the map
$$\varphi^2 : A^2(X) \longrightarrow \mathrm{Gr}'^{\,2}_{\mathrm{top}}(X)$$
an isomorphism for every smooth quasi-projective $X$ (including, e.g., the case $\dim X = 3$)?
artifact.status_search_result: The integral form of the comparison formulas between the Chow ring and the graded of $K'(X)$ for the topological and $\lambda$-filtrations was established by Jouanolou (and, in the surface/threefold setting, by Mumford), removing the "modulo torsion" caveat. In particular $\varphi^2 : A^2(X) \to \mathrm{Gr}'^{\,2}_{\mathrm{top}}(X)$ is known to be an isomorphism. The result is now standard and appears in the literature on Riemann–Roch and the $\gamma$-filtration.

status_evidence.title: Riemann-Roch sans dénominateurs (Jouanolou)
status_evidence.snippet: Jouanolou established Riemann–Roch type formulas for the gamma filtration without neglecting torsion.
status_evidence.claim: Jouanolou proved the integral comparison formulas between A(X) and the graded of K'(X).
